chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Muthannā al-Ḥannāṭ, from al-Ḥasan al-Ṣayqal, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
“The menstruating woman performs ghusl with nine ratls of water.”

Although the apparent wording of this report is the wording of a statement, what is intended by it is a command, since it is impossible that what is intended by it be mere information; for if information had been intended, it would have been false.
And this is like His, the Exalted’s, saying: “And whoever enters it shall be safe.”
Its meaning is only: Grant him safety.

key_terms.تِسْعَةِ أَرْطَالٍ: nine ratls, a specified measure of water
key_terms.كَذِبًا: falsehood, if taken as a literal report

ai.seo_question: How is the hadith about the menstruating woman using nine ratls of water understood in Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This passage states that a menstruating woman performs ghusl with nine ratls of water, then explains that the phrasing should be understood as an imperative rather than a mere report. It also illustrates a principle of interpretation by comparing this usage to a Qur'anic expression whose outward form is informative while its intended meaning is directive.
